title: Outcome-aware exposure scheduler for model version tests
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: We need a lightweight, outcome-aware A/B controller that schedules progressive exposure for new model variants across cohorts while enforcing safety budgets, sequential statistical checks, and automatic rollback when quality regressions are detected. Current rollout primitives are binary (shadow or live) and lack adaptive exposure tied to observed outcome metrics (quality + latency + cost). This ticket defines the product design and acceptance criteria for an exposure scheduler that plugs into the rollout control plane, integrates with Console dashboards and Redwood Optimize signals, and emits clear runbook actions for SREs and PMs.

Goals and scope:
- Allow experiment owners to specify a primary quality metric (or composite metric) and secondary constraints (p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens).
- Support cohort stratification (region, customer tier, device type) and per-cohort exposure caps.
- Implement adaptive exposure ramps using outcome-aware controllers: increase exposure only when sequential checks pass; pause/inverse when degradation signals cross thresholds.
- Provide shadowing sink for mirrored traffic and a burst-only mode for Dedicated pools.
- Define auto-rollback triggers and an alpha-spending sequential test plan to control false positives.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Experiment creation UI accepts: target metric, baseline comparator, initial exposure, max exposure budget, per-cohort caps, audit log URL.
2) Controller evaluates metrics on streaming windows (min 1k samples) and runs sequential checks (optional: alpha spending or Bayesian credible intervals).
3) Controller exposes decisions via Console (decision timeline + rationale) and emits events to the audit log and webhook.
4) Auto-rollback executes when a sustained regression is detected (example: 95% posterior probability new < baseline by > 2% for primary metric AND p95 latency regresses > 30ms for >= 10m).
5) Safety budget enforcement prevents cumulative exposure > configured budget and adds manual approval step if budget exceeded.

Instrumentation and metrics:
- Primary metrics: task-specific quality score (eval-set match rate) and a signal of hallucination rate derived from classifier outputs.
- Operational metrics: p50/p95 latency, CPU/GPU tail utilization, tokens-per-second, cost-per-1k.
- Health metrics: error rate, timeout rate, OOM count.
- Statistical signals: sequential p-value, Bayesian posterior for lift/decline, running CDF of metric deltas.

Integration points and artifacts:
- PRD (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.com/confluence/display/ML/Outcome+Aware+Exposure+Scheduler (proto link)
- Frontend mockups: Drive/Design -> /design/experiments/outcome-aware-scheduler.png
- GitHub spike/POC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-controller/pull/189
- Dashboard proto: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/experiments/PM-271999

Security and compliance:
- No PII is stored by the controller. Audit events include only identifiers and metric aggregates.
- security_review_required: true

Notes on trade-offs:
- Frequent sequential checks reduce time-to-detection but increase false alarms; alpha-spending or Bayesian priors reduce churn at the cost of longer confirmation windows.
- Cohort granularity improves safety but increases required sample size; we recommend starting with 3 cohorts (global, region, enterprise) and expanding.
- Auto-rollback should be conservative for high-value customers; provide opt-out flags per release and require manual approval for rollback in certain account tiers.
